originality.rationale: The accepted claim is the sharp heterogeneous-curvature stationary RR-versus-IID reversal classification, particularly the unique degree-seven algebraic heterogeneity frontier and interval topology. Koloskova et al. (2023), inspected in HTML at sections 3, 5.2 and 6, develop general data-order bounds but their quadratic experiments have one shared Hessian and do not imply the exact stationary heterogeneous phase diagram. Ying et al. (2018), inspected in Sections I and V-A, give exact quadratic stationary expressions for a common design matrix (identical component Hessians), not the unequal-Hessian threshold. Earlier same-curvature RR reversals and two-order stationary optimization do not imply this all-step-size critical ratio. More specialized earlier literature could contain equivalent formulas; publication priority is not independently certified.

value.rationale: The naturally motivated question is whether the widely used without-replacement sampling protocol uniformly improves stationary optimization accuracy over the full individually stable stepsize range, with equal gradient-evaluation budgets. The theorem supplies a sharp, scale-free heterogeneity threshold and exact reversal window, separating a class for which RR dominates at every stable step from a class where its ordering reverses. This mathematically nontrivial parameter boundary, its equality tangency and explicitly certified rational counterexamples can inform interpretation of RR-versus-SGD experiments, without purporting to solve general stochastic optimization.
